title: University of Waterloo researchers create sea cucumber‑inspired gel for tendon repair
content: University of Waterloo researchers have created a gel modeled on sea cucumbers’ capacity to alter body stiffness. The material is designed to assist in repairing damaged tendons and other soft tissues, and it is intended to degrade without leaving permanent material behind.
summary: University of Waterloo researchers designed a gel inspired by sea cucumbers’ ability to alter body stiffness. The gel could one day help repair damaged tendons and other soft tissues without leaving permanent material behind.

title: Scientists rediscover method to make Roman colour‑changing Lycurgus Cup glass
content:
Scientists have announced that they have rediscovered how to reproduce the ancient Roman colour‑changing glass seen in the Lycurgus Cup.  

The Lycurgus Cup, a 1,600‑year‑old masterpiece housed in the British Museum, shifts from jade green under normal lighting to ruby red when illuminated from behind. This dual‑tone effect, described as a feat of optical engineering, has puzzled historians and glass‑makers for centuries.
summary: Scientists have rediscovered the technique used to create the ancient Roman colour‑changing glass seen in the Lycurgus Cup. The 1,600‑year‑old cup in the British Museum appears jade green in normal light and ruby red when lit from behind, a property that has long puzzled experts.
author: Guardian Science

title: APOD October 25, 2026: Dark Matter in a Simulated Universe
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 25 – Dark… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Dark Matter in a Simulated Universe Explanation: Is our universe haunted? It might look that way on this dark matter map. The gravity of unseen dark matter is the leading explanation for why galaxies rotate so fast, why galaxies orbit clusters so fast, why gravitational lenses so strongly deflect light, and how visible matter is distributed. The featured image from the American Museum of Natural History ‘s Hayden Planetarium Space Show, Dark Universe, highlights one example of how pervasive dark matter might haunt our universe. In this frame from a detailed computer simulation, complex filaments of dark matter, shown in black, are strewn about the universe like spider webs, while the relatively rare clumps of familiar baryon ic matter are colored orange. These simulations are good statistical matches to astronomical observations. In what is perhaps a scarier turn of events, dark matter — although quite strange and in an unknown form — is no longer thought to be the strangest source of gravity in the universe. That honor now falls to dark energy, a more uniform source of repulsive gravity that seems to now dominate the expansion of the entire universe. summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day for October 25, 2026 features a computer simulation of dark‑matter filaments (black) and baryonic matter clumps (orange) from the American Museum of Natural History’s Hayden Planetarium “Dark Universe” show. The caption notes that dark energy, not dark matter, is now considered the most mysterious source of gravity.

title: Lara Croft turns 30; article reviews the video game icon’s biggest blunders
content: We all know the highlights of the tomb raider’s storied career – but what about the lowlights? We dig deep to unearth the archaeologist’s less glorious moments Happy birthday, Lara! This month marks 30 years since Ms Croft first swan-dived into our lives with her unique blend of athletic prowess, archaeological expertise and giant knockers. More than 100 million Tomb Raider games have been sold since. We all remember the good times: the bold design and sheer playability of the original titles; the establishment of Lara as a 90s icon, embodying both lads’ mag culture and girl power; the way she made games cool, even appearing on the cover of the Face. We’ve had blockbuster movies, big budget reboots, and shiny reissues. And who could forget the time we got to powerwash her house? But no one gets to 30 without a few skeletons in the closet – or in Lara’s case, butlers in the freezer. So here’s a look at the darker parts of her past.
summary: Lara Croft turned 30 this month, three decades after her debut, and more than 100 million Tomb Raider games have been sold. The piece looks at the darker parts of her past and highlights the series’ biggest blunders alongside its movies, reboots and reissues.

title: Cookie theft enables fraudsters to hijack bank sessions and access accounts
content:
Cookie theft, also known as session hijacking, occurs when fraudsters target “session cookies” to gain unauthorized access to user accounts. These digital keys allow attackers to hijack and use accounts without the user’s knowledge.

After a typical morning of logging into various accounts to check balances and make payments, a user may close their laptop and move on to other tasks. However, the session with the bank can still be hijacked by fraudsters, who then gain access to the account. The user becomes a victim of cookie theft, a form of session hijacking.
summary: Session cookies are a primary target for hackers because they allow account hijacking. The theft of these cookies, known as session hijacking, lets fraudsters access a bank account after a user logs in and closes their laptop.

content:

Demonstrations in Paris began peacefully but ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrests nationwide, according to France 24 International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry.

title: France sees 410,000 protesters, CGT says nearly double
content:
More than 400,000 people protested across France on Saturday in largely peaceful demonstrations, easing fears of a repeat of the violence seen the previous weekend. Participants, including students, workers, and retirees, marched to demand action on the rising cost of living and increased funding for public services. The government estimated nationwide turnout at 410,000, while the CGT union claimed the figure was nearly twice as high.

Many protesters indicated that their anger shows no sign of fading. The demonstrations highlighted a broad coalition of groups united in their demands for economic relief and better public service support.
summary: Saturday's demonstrations across France were largely peaceful and drew hundreds of thousands of people demanding action on the rising cost of living and more funding for public services. The government reported a nationwide turnout of 410,000, while the CGT union estimated the figure was almost twice as high.

Prosecutors said the attack is believed to have been motivated by racism, noting that most victims were of foreign origin.

title: Study finds pre-pack phoenix deals see higher repeat failures and lower creditor payouts
content:
A Guardian‑commissioned study finds that companies revived through “pre‑pack” administrations, where former management takes over the business, tend to pay creditors far less than other insolvency routes. The research also shows that these pre‑pack deals are much more likely to end in failure again.

The study highlights the broader practice of “phoenixism” – liquidating a company to allow its directors to restart with a new entity that carries no debts. It notes a boss whose business has failed twice but appears to be back, underscoring the recurring risks associated with this approach.
summary: Research for the Guardian found that insolvent businesses reacquired by their former managers in pre‑pack administrations are much more likely to fail again. The same study showed these deals also repay far less to creditors, prompting renewed scrutiny of phoenix practices.

title: Storm Boelo brings 80mph gusts to Scotland, N.Ireland and northern England
content:

Storm Boelo was the second named storm in as many days, following Storm Austen, which brought strong winds to parts of the UK on Friday. An amber warning zone was activated at 9 p.m. on Saturday for the regions experiencing the high winds.
summary: Storm Boelo produced gusts of 80 mph in exposed coastal spots and wind speeds of 60‑70 mph across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England. The Met Office issued an amber warning at 9 pm on Saturday and advised people in the affected areas to stay indoors.

title: Palestinians fear Gaza's plight ignored in Israel election campaign
content:
Israel’s upcoming election has drawn little attention to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.  Rival candidates Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu have pledged to end Hamas rule, yet the campaign has largely ignored the dire conditions faced by the territory’s residents.  

Palestinians in Gaza, where nearly a million displaced people endure severe sanitary problems, water shortages and a persistent threat of Israeli strikes, are bracing for an outcome that could determine their future.  The region has been reduced to rubble and has suffered almost 75,000 deaths, a reality that remains largely absent from the election discourse.
summary: Rivals Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu have vowed to end Hamas rule as Israel prepares for a poll. Palestinians in Gaza, where nearly a million displaced face dire sanitary conditions, water shortages and the threat of Israeli strikes, say the humanitarian catastrophe that has killed nearly 75,000 people is largely absent from the election campaign.

title: The Narco Hack review – an epic tale of how detectives’ tech wizardry smashed a billion-euro drugs ring
content:
The Narco Hack is a three-part documentary that chronicles a joint investigation by French, Belgian, and Dutch police forces. The series details how these agencies compromised the encryption software of the Sky ECC app to undermine several massive criminal organizations. The narrative begins with a 2020 audio recording of a call to French police, where two men report their car is being attacked by gunfire. During the exchange, one caller shouts that he is going to die, and the footage reveals that his companion, a mechanic named Houcine Hakkar, was killed.

The documentary highlights that this specific killing had been planned and discussed in detail on the Sky ECC platform. By infiltrating the app’s security, law enforcement officers gained access to the communications of these criminal groups. The review describes the investigation as a blend of modern technological methods and human heroism, comparing the tone to the television series The Wire and the film The Imitation Game. The story illustrates how detectives used technical expertise to dismantle a billion-euro drugs ring through an approach that was both logical and complex.
summary: Human heroism is celebrated in profoundly personal ways in this extraordinary tale of a mind-boggling investigation into massive criminal organisations. It’s part The Wire, part The Imitation Game We begin with the audio of a horrifying call made to the French police in 2020.

title: The Snowman stage show gets hi-tech reboot with new Santa
content:
Director Will Tuckett and Paddington designer Tahra Zafar have refreshed the stage adaptation of Raymond Briggs’ The Snowman, more than three decades after the original 1993 production. The reboot, which has been an annual outing for Birmingham Rep since its inception, features a new musical arrangement by director Andy Massey and introduces a “hunky” Saint Nick character to the cast.

Tuckett, a former Royal Ballet dancer who has directed productions including the National Ballet of Japan’s Nutcracker, leads the creative team for this updated version. The production utilizes innovative staging, demonstrated in a Birmingham studio where a large wooden box opens like a book cover to reveal a house set. This set includes a kitchen with a couple and a puppet cat, as well as an upstairs area where a boy wakes up in anticipation of Christmas.
summary: Director Will Tuckett and designer Tahra Zafar are refreshing the long-running stage adaptation of Raymond Briggs’ classic story. The production features a new hunky Saint Nick character and high-tech set pieces for its upcoming run.

title: The Stone Roses showed me the power of being an introvert
content: At boarding school in the early 90s, quietness was seen as weakness. But then I saw the band’s guitarist John Squire making a vast noise while hiding behind a fringe – and learned the strength of understatement In September 1991, I had just been thrown into the meat-grinder of a Midlands boarding school. In this bear pit, there were predators and there was prey. You were either the swaggering rugby alpha, whipping a wet towel at pale bodies in the eight-boy dormitory; or the homesick ghost, keeping your guard up, endlessly braced for your toilet cubicle to be kicked open or your washbag chucked off the fire escape. My mind had always been loud, racing with opinions, stories, jokes. But by the time I adequately considered a thought, the conversation had raced on without me. Suddenly, under 24/7 social scrutiny in a world where bullhorn confidence is king, I felt dismissed.
summary: At boarding school in the early 90s, quietness was seen as weakness. But then I saw the band’s guitarist John Squire making a vast noise while hiding behind a fringe – and learned the strength of understatement In September 1991, I had just been thrown into the meat-grinder of a Midlands boarding school.

title: Marlon James and Nicholas Boggs discuss life as literary power couple
content: Shortlisted for the Booker and Baillie Gifford prizes respectively, the novelist and biographer talk about working and living together – and giving a voice to Black queer history The literary power couple is a historically seductive concept. Two writers sharing a life, their private and creative worlds entwined, each becoming witness to and critic of the other’s work. Think Simone de Beauvoir and Jean-Paul Sartre, Joan Didion and John Gregory Dunne. Or, less auspiciously, Sylvia Plath and Ted Hughes. Now, into this illustrious company steps a new pair: the novelist Marlon James and the biographer Nicholas Boggs, whose books have each been shortlisted for one of Britain’s most prestigious literary awards – James for the Booker prize and Boggs for the Baillie Gifford prize for nonfiction. Between them, they have produced two formidable books, each the culmination of years of work, and each concerned with the lives of Black queer men whose stories have often been overlooked.
summary: Novelist Marlon James and biographer Nicholas Boggs are shortlisted for the Booker and Baillie Gifford prizes, respectively. They discuss their partnership and their books, which focus on the lives of Black queer men.

title: Siobhán McSweeney becomes presenter of Guardian's Comfort Eating podcast
content: The Derry Girls actor has always loved food, so who better to take over as the new presenter of the Guardian’s Comfort Eating podcast? Siobhán McSweeney is teaching me her preferred way to enjoy a packet of cheese and onion crisps. She has arranged two matching slabs of Cadbury’s Dairy Milk chocolate, two piles of Tayto crisps and two cans of Guinness on the table in front of us – and is issuing strict instructions. “Don’t swallow!” she booms theatrically, and I freeze, my mouth full of Taytos. The trick, McSweeney explains, is to get the crisps, chocolate and Guinness into your mouth at the same time, and then swill it all around a bit to make a kind of boozy, oniony soup. “See?” McSweeney is watching me carefully to check I am putting all the ingredients into my mouth in the correct order. “It’s delicious! Just delicious!” McSweeney burst into the public consciousness back in 2018 with Derry Girls, a comedy series about a group of Catholic schoolgirls, set against the background of the Troubles in 1990s Northern Ireland. McSweeney won a Bafta playing the girls’ headmistress, Sister Michael – a potty-mouthed, judo-loving nun – and can count Martin Scorsese as a fan. Asked for a TV recommendation during a panel discussion in 2022, the director name-checked Derry Girls and then lifted his fist in the air in a kind of salute, exclaiming rapturously, “Those nuns!”

title: UK Secures Belgium Pipeline Deal Amid 60% Gas Import Reliance
content:
Britain’s gas security remains a concern, even after the recent approval of the Jackdaw field in the North Sea. The United Kingdom still imports almost 60 % of its gas, and the new field has not eliminated the country’s supply and resilience issues.

In response, the UK has secured a last‑minute arrangement with Belgium to allow sufficient gas to flow through a connecting pipeline during the winter. The deal is described as a “belt‑and‑braces” measure that would activate only if a “low‑probability but high‑impact stress event” occurs. Such an event, while potentially severe, may never materialise.

The arrangement also highlights the vulnerability of key infrastructure, such as the two import terminals in Milford Haven that bring liquefied natural gas (LNG) into Britain. title: Hammersmith Bridge is a symbol of our dysfunctional times. The money is there, the joined-up thinking isn’t | Simon Jenkins
content:
Simon Jenkins argues that London’s Hammersmith Bridge serves as a metaphor for the dysfunction within the British government. The bridge, which has been closed to motor traffic and inert for seven years, is described as a victim of administrative anarchy. Its closure, combined with the current shutdown of the Albert Bridge, has resulted in 37,000 extra vehicles attempting to cross the River Thames, bringing south London close to perpetual gridlock.

Jenkins contrasts London’s status as the richest and smartest place in Britain with its apparent poor management, likening its operation to a high street vape shop. He cites slowing buses, increasing homelessness, and longer hospital waiting times as evidence of this decline. Additionally, he highlights a lack of decisive policy, noting the inability to determine whether to build an HS2 terminus or a Heathrow runway.

The columnist also criticizes a recent decision by a "robotic Whitehall algorithm" to increase Kensington’s annual housing target to 5,107 homes, up from the previous target of 1,381. Jenkins characterizes this jump as ludicrous, using it to underscore his broader argument that while funding exists, the necessary coordinated thinking is absent from public administration.
summary: London’s roads are horrendous, with constant roadworks and creaking infrastructure. And the emblem of all that spans the River Thames London’s Hammersmith Bridge is a metaphor for all that is wrong with British government.

title: Emily Bratt Calls for Japan‑Style Civic Pride to Curb UK Antisocial Behaviour

But while I welcome his policy to fine “headphone dodgers”, I’m not convinced it will solve the problem. This behaviour isn’t only a nuisance, but a grave indicator of a deeper societal issue: the erosion of empathy. You can’t legislate civic pride into an individualistic culture where feelings of social disconnection are widespread.
summary: Emily Bratt, who worked in Japanese schools, says teaching civic pride creates adults who consider others. She argues that the UK’s plan to fine “headphone dodgers” will not solve antisocial behaviour, which she views as a sign of societal erosion of empathy.

title: V-2 rocket captures first photos of Earth from space in 1946
content:
On October 24, 1946, a U.S. Army V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico captured the first-ever photograph of Earth from space. The rocket carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that recorded a new frame every second and a half. It reached an altitude of approximately 65 miles before re-entering the atmosphere. The rocket and camera were destroyed upon impact at a speed of about 340 miles per hour, but the film survived because it was housed in a steel case. Scientists retrieved the film from the New Mexico desert and reportedly jumped up and down with joy upon seeing the grainy, black-and-white images for the first time.

The successful capture of these images marked a significant milestone, as no one had previously seen Earth from space. This capability drove increased interest in space exploration and led to societal shifts in how humanity viewed its home planet. For military and intelligence agencies, the event demonstrated the potential for large-scale reconnaissance, a capability far exceeding that of high-altitude aircraft. This technological advancement eventually expanded into agriculture and meteorological applications, making Earth observation one of the most common reasons for deploying satellites and space stations today. Furthermore, viewing the planet as a "blue marble" against a black void highlighted its fragility, contributing to the birth of the environmental movement.
summary: V-2 rocket captures first photos of Earth from space in 1946.

summary: Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season ended against Aston Villa. This result leaves manager Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.

title: José Andrés Takes Stand Against Washington Foie Gras Ban
content: World-renowned chef José Andrés has entered the debate over Washington’s proposed ban on foie gras, a delicacy described by animal rights activists as cruel. Andrés responded to a proponent of Initiative 86, which appears on D.C.’s ballot, via a post on the social platform X, arguing in favor of serving the French dish.
summary: Chef José Andrés has entered the debate over Washington’s proposed foie gras ban, Initiative 86. He posted on X in response to a proponent of the ban, arguing about serving the French delicacy.

title: Trump attends Hannity-Earhardt wedding rehearsal dinner at Mar-a-Lago
content: Fox News hosts Sean Hannity and Ainsley Earhardt celebrated their wedding rehearsal dinner on Friday evening at President Trump’s Mar‑a‑Lago club in Palm Beach, Fla. Trump and first lady Melania Trump, along with other top Trump administration officials, were present, while the president is not expected to attend the wedding.

content: Bill Maher, a left-leaning comedian and talk show host, told former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt he actually likes President Trump’s proposed ballroom in the East Wing, despite frequent criticism from Democrats. “I don’t give a s— about any of this. I like the ballroom. America does need a ballroom,” Maher told Leavitt in…

title: Ro Khanna Wrong About European Chaos and JD Vance
content: Protests that began in France last week escalated into widespread looting and arson, with thousands of businesses destroyed. The unrest, described as organized far‑left anarchy, saw participants engaging in chaotic acts that left many establishments burned to the ground.

title: MAHA Drives Surge of Doctors Running for Congress and State Offices
content: Dozens of medical professionals are running for Congress and top state offices in this midterm season, a direct Democrat‑led counteraction to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) agenda’s outsized influence on national health policy. Seven physicians are running for congressional office, including Democrats Abdul El‑Sayed of Michigan, Annie Andrews of South Carolina, and Amish Shah.

title: NFL shuts Paris fan zone after protests, Saints-Steelers game stays on Sunday
content: The NFL shut its Paris fan zone on Saturday after intense street protests, notifying fans through the league’s OnePass app. Despite President Trump’s suggestion to delay the matchup, the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers remain scheduled to play the league’s first game in France on Sunday.
summary: The NFL closed its Paris fan zone on Saturday because of intense street protests. The New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers remain scheduled to play the league’s first game in France on Sunday, despite President Trump suggesting a postponement.
author: The Hill

title: Triple-action weight-loss drug reduces sleep apnea in late-stage trials
content:
A new triple-action weekly weight-loss drug has demonstrated an ability to reduce sleep apnea in two late-stage clinical trials. The condition, often dismissed as simple snoring, involves repeated pauses in breathing throughout the night that degrade sleep quality.

Untreated sleep apnea causes significant drops in blood oxygen levels during sleep. These disruptions can lead to serious long-term health consequences beyond morning grogginess, highlighting the importance of effective treatment options.
summary: A triple-action weekly weight-loss drug has been shown to reduce sleep apnea in two late-stage trials. The condition causes repeated breathing pauses during sleep that can negatively impact long-term health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 10 years after Ebola: Lab partnership boosts viral hemorrhagic fever diagnostics in Guinea
content: Researchers in Guinea have established a laboratory partnership to enhance diagnostics for viral hemorrhagic fevers, marking a decade since the Ebola outbreak in West Africa. Leveraging nearly a decade of surveillance data, the team documents the regional burden of Lassa fever. They explain that sustainable diagnostic structures support prevention efforts and help reduce the risk of major viral outbreaks.
summary: The researchers used nearly a decade of surveillance to document the burden of Lassa fever in the region. They explain that sustainable diagnostic structures can support prevention and reduce the risk of major viral outbreaks.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Nanoscale alloy redesign tackles cold brittleness for potential deep-space and deep-sea applications
content: Traditional metallic alloys face significant challenges in ultralow temperature environments, where they often experience performance degradation due to a persistent trade-off between strength, ductility, and toughness. While metals may gain strength at lower temperatures, they simultaneously become more brittle and susceptible to fracture. These limitations hinder their use in critical applications such as aerospace, clean energy, superconducting systems, and deep-space exploration, which require materials to maintain high strength, ductility, and fracture toughness under extreme cold.
summary: A nanoscale alloy redesign aims to reduce cold brittleness for deep-space and deep-sea use. Traditional alloys lose strength, ductility, and toughness at ultralow temperatures, becoming more brittle and prone to fracture.
author: Phys.org

title: New Protein Pathway Allows HIV to Hide in Cells Despite Treatment
content: Newly identified protein pathways allow HIV to remain dormant within specific immune cells and the brain, despite effective blood-suppressing treatments. These hidden viral reservoirs persist even when medications control the virus in the bloodstream, serving as the primary obstacle to achieving a cure with current therapies.
summary: Current HIV medicines suppress the virus in the blood, but HIV can remain dormant in certain immune cells and the brain. These hidden reservoirs prevent a cure with today's treatments.
author: Phys.org

title: One-positron cyclotron could test Standard Model prediction
content: The positron, the antimatter counterpart of the electron, shares the electron’s mass but carries an opposite electric charge. Like the electron, it behaves as a tiny bar magnet. A key prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics states that the positron’s magnetic moment should be exactly equal and opposite to that of the electron.
summary: The positron is the antimatter counterpart of the electron, identical in mass but carrying an opposite electric charge. A one-positron cyclotron could test the Standard Model prediction that the positron's magnetic moment is exactly equal and opposite to the electron's.
author: Phys.org

title: Flare Ribbons Reveal Hidden Solar Explosions on the Sun
content: The article explains how flare ribbons can reveal hidden solar explosions on the sun. It notes that many astronomy topics are esoteric and that there is little direct connection between a supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way and everyday life. However, the sun is different: its presence is inescapable, and its behavior—especially its flaring—has a noticeable impact on us.
summary: Flare ribbons reveal hidden solar explosions on the sun. The sun's flaring has an impact on everyday life.
author: Phys.org

title: Glioblastoma fluid makes cancer cells more invasive, persists after removal
content: Scientists have found that the thick, sticky fluid surrounding glioblastoma tumors can alter cancer cells, making them smaller, more flexible, and more capable of invading nearby tissue. Remarkably, some of these changes remain even after the cells leave the fluid, uncovering a previously overlooked mechanism that may facilitate the spread of this deadly cancer.
summary: Scientists found that the thick, sticky fluid around glioblastoma tumors can make brain cancer cells smaller, more flexible, and better at invading surrounding tissue. Some of these changes persist after the cells leave the fluid, revealing a previously overlooked mechanism that could help the cancer spread.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find protein switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
content:
Scientists discovered that turning off a protein called Mitch causes human cells to burn more fat and stops new fat cells from forming.  

The finding follows mouse studies that showed resistance to obesity and better muscular endurance, offering hope for a new weight‑loss treatment.
summary: Scientists discovered that turning off the protein Mitch causes human cells to burn more fat and prevents the development of new fat cells. The discovery builds on mouse experiments that showed resistance to obesity and improved muscular endurance, suggesting a new weight‑loss approach.
author: Science Daily

title: LG C6 OLED TV on Sale with $400 Discount Ahead of Black Friday
content:
LG has begun its early Black Friday promotion, offering its C6 OLED TV at discounted prices through November 1. The 55‑inch model is available for $999.99, a $400 reduction from its regular price, with Amazon and Best Buy matching the offer. The 65‑inch version is on sale for $1,399.99, a $300 discount, also available at Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from LG. A 77‑inch C6 can be purchased for $1,999.99 from Amazon, down from $2,499.99. Purchases made directly from LG include a free Xbox Wireless Controller and a complimentary wall mount.

The C6 builds on last year’s C5 with several upgrades. It features the Alpha 11 AI Gen3 processor, which improves picture and sound quality, and a brighter display. The refresh rate is increased to 165 Hz, up from 144 Hz, and the TV retains four HDMI 2.1 ports with support for AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G‑Sync. OLED technology delivers deep blacks, vibrant color, and high contrast. The TV supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, and it has built‑in streaming apps such as Netflix and HBO Max. Google Cast, Apple AirPlay 2, and Matter support enable easy content sharing and smart‑home integration.

LG has addressed recent concerns about data collection on its smart TVs. The company states that its TVs do not continuously record conversations and that voice‑recognition and interest‑based advertising features are optional and disabled by default. While some data‑collection practices remain under scrutiny, they do not affect the C6’s feature set.
summary: LG’s C6 OLED TV is on sale in multiple sizes starting at $999.99 ($300 off). | Image: LG Black Friday is still over a month away, but if you’re hoping to upgrade your TV, you don’t need to wait until November.
author: The Verge

title: Fielded Evolves from Experimental Noise to Restless R&B with 2020 Album
content:
Lindsay Powell, who releases music under the name Fielded, has built a career around subverting expectations and genre conventions. According to her Bandcamp page, Fielded began as an experimental noise project before evolving into a sound closer to R&B, but the artist has always approached the genre with a restless, boundary‑pushing attitude.

Fielded’s debut album, Ninety‑Thirty‑Thirty, features tracks heavily indebted to ’80s synth‑pop and includes multiple saxophone solos. The follow‑up, Boy Angel, is described as a quirky electronic exploration that uses huge saw‑wave synths, jittery percussion, and sky‑high vocal stacks. In 2020, the artist released Demisexual Lovelace, continuing her exploration of unconventional musical forms.
summary: Fielded Evolves from Experimental Noise to Restless R&B with 2020 Album.
author: The Verge

title: Study finds Grok AI favors Republicans, OpenAI GPT favors Democrats in 500 races
content:
A new study compared the political recommendations of two AI models, Grok and OpenAI's GPT.

The study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommended Republican candidates, while GPT favored Democrats. The models disagreed in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.
summary: A new study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommends Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats. The two AI models disagreed in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.

title: Developers unveil cassette, notebook, flight tracker, toaster apps for iPhone Duo
content: Developers are releasing a range of inventive apps—such as retro cassette‑player simulations, virtual notebooks, flight‑tracking tools and a digital toaster—to demonstrate the capabilities of Apple’s first foldable device, the iPhone Duo. These creations highlight how the new form factor can be leveraged for diverse user experiences.
summary: Developers are creating retro cassette player, virtual notebook, flight tracker and digital toaster apps for Apple’s first foldable iPhone. These apps showcase creative ways to take advantage of the iPhone Duo’s capabilities.

title: Two critical PHP bugs threatened to upend the internet
content: Two critical bugs were discovered in the PHP web programming language, which powers the majority of the internet. According to the report, these vulnerabilities threatened to upend the internet, and analysts note that similar major software scares are unlikely to be the last.
summary: Two critical bugs were discovered in the PHP web programming language. The bugs, in a language used by the majority of the internet, threatened to upend the internet and may not be the last major software scare.

title: Lula and Flavio rally across Brazil as polls show neck‑and‑neck race ahead of Sunday election
content: Lula and Flavio, the two contenders in Brazil’s second‑round presidential election, are holding rallies in major cities on the final day of campaigning. Approximately 20 % of voters abstained in the first round, leaving the outcome uncertain, while opinion polls indicate the candidates are neck‑and‑neck ahead of Sunday’s vote.
summary: Lula and Flavio, the two candidates in Brazil’s second‑round presidential election, held rallies in major cities on the final day of campaigning. Around 20% of voters abstained in the first round, leaving the race wide open with opinion polls showing the candidates neck and neck.

title: France protests see police use tear gas as hundreds of thousands rally
content:
Demonstrations continued across France on Saturday, with protesters rallying around purchasing‑power concerns and the defence of public services. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris, a slight drop from the 550,000 who marched the previous week. The union that organised the authorised events put the total at 800,000 participants across the country, with 250,000 in the capital.

Clashes broke out in Paris, Lyon, Rennes, Nantes, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille, and police fired tear‑gas at demonstrators during the confrontations.
summary: The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, focusing on purchasing power and the defence of public services. Clashes broke out in cities such as Paris, Lyon, Rennes, Nantes, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille, and police fired tear gas at demonstrators.

title: France to Deploy 70,000 Police for Nationwide Yellow Vest, Union, Student March
content: A coalition of the “Yellow Vests” movement, trade unions and students plans to march across France on Saturday, citing concerns about studying conditions and purchasing power. Authorities anticipate deploying about 70,000 police officers nationwide, warning of possible looting and vandalism reminiscent of unrest that occurred the previous Saturday.
summary: A coalition of Yellow Vests, trade unions and students will march across France on Saturday demanding better studying conditions and purchasing power. Authorities fear looting and vandalism similar to last Saturday's unrest and expect to deploy some 70,000 police officers nationwide.
author: France 24

title: Italy deploys 500 soldiers to Milan amid new cost of living protests
content:
Soldiers were deployed across Milan and luxury boutiques boarded up as protesters took to the streets again on Saturday, a week after looting and clashes with police.  

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced a series of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to the city and introducing tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large proportion of last week’s violent protesters. Surveillance helicopters circled central Piazza del Duomo, while soldiers patrolled in groups alongside military vehicles and a water cannon.  

Some visitors said they would leave the city centre if violence broke out again. Our Rome correspondent, Seema Gupta, has the latest.
summary: Italy deploys 500 soldiers to Milan amid new cost of living protests.

title: Israel begins demolitions in Hebron after attack that killed two soldiers, 1,200 displaced
content: The Palestinian Authority has called for international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official reported that approximately 1,200 residents of Hebron in the West Bank were forced to leave their homes. This displacement followed a Friday attack that killed two Israeli soldiers. The head of Hebron's municipality stated that an additional 1,300 people may also be compelled to vacate their homes.
summary: The Palestinian Authority urged international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official said around 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron were forced to leave their homes following an attack on Friday that killed two Israeli soldiers. The head of Hebron's municipality said an additional 1,300 may also be forced to leave.

title: France protests draw over 400,000 participants, clashes break out in cities
content:
The Ministry of the Interior said at least 410,000 people took part in Saturday’s protests across France, including 110,000 in Paris, to demand action on the high cost of living. Other reports put the total number of demonstrators at nearly 800,000 nationwide and 250,000 in the capital.

title: Yemen's Houthi rebels claim attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports
content: Yemen’s Iran‑allied Houthi rebels said they carried out attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday. The Saudi‑backed Yemeni government reported that the group also launched three ballistic missiles at coast‑guard sites in the port city of Aden.

title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
content: Turkey and Libya have announced plans to redraw their Mediterranean maritime boundaries as part of a new economic corridor. The proposal has provoked strong protests from Greece and has drawn the European Union into the dispute, intensifying tensions between the parties.
summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

title: Chancellor John Healey announces £7m fund for northern England Olympic feasibility study
content: John Healey will announce a £7 million fund in his first budget as chancellor to examine a potential future Olympic bid for northern England. The money is earmarked for a full feasibility study that would assess the possibility of hosting the Games in the north of England in the 2040s. The campaign for a northern Olympics has the backing of northern mayors and top athletes, who support the study’s aim to determine whether a future bid could be successful.
summary: John Healey will announce a £7 million fund in his first budget as chancellor to examine a possible Olympic bid for northern England. The money will finance a full feasibility study for Games that could be held in the north of England in the 2040s and is supported by northern mayors and leading athletes.

title: Sam Fender says high ticket prices for Proper Massive stadium tour will be lowered
content: Fender criticises stadium pricing, calling it ‘bollocks’ and says it ‘won’t be happening’ on his tour Sam Fender has responded to criticism by fans about ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising he would lower the cost, telling followers on Instagram: “They’re getting changed.” The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive stadium tour earlier this week.
summary: Sam Fender says high ticket prices for Proper Massive stadium tour will be lowered.

title: Ukraine military reports stable Starlink connection after recent speed restrictions
content:
Ukraine’s military announced that its connection to the Starlink satellite communications system is now stable, ten days after a sudden restriction limited its use. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked U.S. allies for restoring the system, which he described as essential for air‑defence and frontline logistics.

Starlink terminals, built by SpaceX and overseen by the U.S. government, are a key component of Ukrainian military operations. The earlier speed restriction capped terminal performance at 160 km/h (99 mph) and caused the failure of several combat missions earlier in the month.
summary: Ukraine’s military said it now has a stable connection to the Starlink satellite communications system, ten days after the service was suddenly restricted. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked US allies for restoring the system, which SpaceX provides and the US government manages, after speed caps of 160 km/h had caused several combat missions to fail.
author: Guardian World

title: Hundreds of thousands march across France protesting school conditions and policing
content:
Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests supporting schoolchildren’s calls for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated school buildings. Government estimates put participation at at least 400,000 people, while trade unions claim the figure is double that, occurring as President Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months in office.

In Paris, government estimates recorded at least 110,000 demonstrators marching along the city’s eastern edge. Protesters also voiced concerns about the high cost of living and the government’s heavy policing, alleging that riot police had been deployed to target school protesters over the past month rather than offering political solutions.
summary: Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests supporting schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and building repairs. Government estimates put participation at at least 400,000 nationwide, including at least 110,000 in Paris, while trade unions claim the number was double.
author: Guardian World

title: Portsmouth beat Millwall 2-1 with Waddingham's late deflected winner
content:
Thomas Waddingham secured a late, fortunate 2-1 victory for Portsmouth against Millwall at Fratton Park. The winning goal came in the 82nd minute when Jake Cooper’s attempted clearance ricocheted off Waddingham and into the net, settling an error-strewn contest. Millwall had taken an early lead through Jenson Metcalfe following a mistake by Portsmouth goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid, but Lyndon Dykes quickly equalized with an own goal.

In other Championship action, Norwich City returned to winning ways with a 3-1 victory over Charton.
summary: Thomas Waddingham scored a fortunate 82nd-minute winner as Portsmouth defeated Millwall 2-1 at Fratton Park. The match featured errors from both sides, including a goal from Jenson Metcalfe and an own goal by Lyndon Dykes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: US gymnast Fred Richard wins first world floor title in Rotterdam
content:
American Frederick Richard claimed his first world gymnastics title by winning the floor exercise at the championships in Rotterdam on Saturday. The 22-year-old secured the gold medal with a score of 14.633, edging out Britain’s Jake Jarman by 0.033 points. Israel’s Artem Dolgopyat also competed in the final, with Jarman, the defending world champion, finishing second in a field that included the last two Olympic gold medallists.

Richard’s victory marks a significant milestone as he becomes the first US man to win floor gold at the world championships since 2003. US gymnastics great Simone Biles was present in the Netherlands as a spectator, watching the American claim the world title.
summary: US gymnast Fred Richard wins first world floor title in Rotterdam.
author: Guardian Sport

title: ‘It feels like a fairy tale’: American Paula Moltzan wins first World Cup race by 0.01sec
content:
American Paula Moltzan secured her first Alpine skiing World Cup victory on Saturday in a season-opening giant slalom at Sölden, Austria. The 32-year-old became the oldest woman to claim such a win, finishing with a combined time of 2 minutes 14.82 seconds. Moltzan, who was fifth after the opening run, delivered a strong second descent to edge out Albania’s Lara Colturi, who finished in 2 minutes 14.83 seconds.

The narrow margin of victory was just one-hundredth of a second. Germany’s Emma Aicher completed the podium, finishing 0.52 seconds behind the Minnesota native. Meanwhile, Mikaela Shiffrin dropped from first to seventh place during the competition.
summary: ‘It feels like a fairy tale’: American Paula Moltzan wins first World Cup race by 0.01sec.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Aston Villa and Jackson end Manchester City’s perfect run with stunning win
content:
Aston Villa defeated Manchester City in the Premier League, ending the visitors’ perfect on-pitch record. Nicolas Jackson scored a double to secure the win for his side against Erling Haaland. The match marked Manchester City’s fourth consecutive loss at this venue, highlighting their fallibility after a strong start.

The result was influenced by errors from Manchester City defenders Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who contributed to Jackson’s goals. This victory concluded the perfect start for Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca, proving that their initial seven-game run was not guaranteed to continue.
summary: Manchester City have added a loss in the Premier League to the one to the Premier League, as their perfect on-pitch record vanished at Aston Villa. The two most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side come out on top against Erling Haaland.

content: Defending champions Australia defeated a new-look England side at the Women's Rugby League World Cup, ending England's hopes of closing the gap between the two teams. summary: A new-look England side failed to close the gap on Australia during the Women's Rugby League World Cup. The defending champions dismantled England, dashing their hopes of getting closer to the top team.

title: England beat France 82-0 in Perth to stay in World Cup contention
content: England defeated France 82-0 in Perth, maintaining their World Cup qualification hopes. To advance to the semi-finals, England must defeat Papua New Guinea on Friday, while Tonga is required to beat Samoa next Sunday.
summary: England defeated France 82-0 in Perth to keep their World Cup hopes alive. They must beat Papua New Guinea and require Tonga to defeat Samoa to reach the semi-finals.

content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Saturday that the country’s Starlink satellite links have been restored following a period of access limitations. SpaceX’s military-grade version of the service, known as Starshield, supports Ukraine’s drone operations and communication networks.
summary: Ukraine’s Starlink satellite links have been restored after limitations were experienced. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the restoration, noting that SpaceX’s Starshield supports drone operations and communication.

summary: President Trump pushed back Saturday morning against reports he was considering replacing the White House press briefing room with an indoor swimming pool. content: The Department of Justice announced on Friday that federal authorities arrested 42-year-old Ian Brinksman, a government contractor, and charged him with leaking classified national defense information. summary: Federal authorities arrested 42‑year‑old Ian Brinksman, a government contractor, and charged him with leaking classified national defense information. title: Economic populism rises in both parties as voters seek financial stability solutions
content: A new form of economic populism is gaining momentum within both political parties this year. This shift occurs as voters seek a party capable of addressing their increasing concerns regarding financial stability.

title: Creating 'satellite maps' of thousands of proteins across tissue could transform drug therapies
content: A new technology generates thousands of detailed "satellite maps" that illustrate where individual proteins are located and distributed across entire tissues in the body or brain. Much like a satellite provides a full picture of Earth, this innovation offers a comprehensive view of protein distribution within biological systems.
summary: A new technology can generate thousands of detailed satellite maps that show the location and distribution of individual proteins across an entire tissue in the body or brain. These maps could transform drug therapies.
